query: For magnetic high-entropy alloys, what single intervention could increase the coercive field? State one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention, the mechanism expected to alter coercivity, the predicted outcome relative to a matched baseline, the conditions under which the effect should hold, the prior evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an experiment with a clear result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: The addition of 1 at.% B and subsequent aging at 600°C for 10 hours will increase the coercive field of the FeCoNiCrMn magnetic high-entropy alloy by 30% relative to the baseline alloy without B addition.
generation.intervention: Addition of 1 at.% B and subsequent aging at 600°C for 10 hours
generation.conditions: Magnetic field applied parallel to the aging direction
generation.mechanism: Pinning of magnetic domain walls by boride precipitates, increasing the energy required for domain wall motion
generation.predicted_outcome: Increase in coercive field by 30% relative to the baseline alloy without B addition
generation.baseline: FeCoNiCrMn magnetic high-entropy alloy without B addition
generation.boundary: The effect of boride precipitates on coercivity may be limited by the formation of other microstructural features that can pin magnetic domain walls
generation.uncertainty: The actual increase in coercive field may vary depending on the specific conditions of B addition and aging, as well as the resulting microstructure

falsification_experiment.design: Measure the coercive field of the FeCoNiCrMn magnetic high-entropy alloy with and without B addition and aging, using a standardized protocol for magnetic property measurement
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coercive field of the alloy with B addition and aging is not significantly higher than that of the baseline alloy, the hypothesis is falsified
